methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
AheadComputing is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $51.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 private and public peers in Chips & Semiconductors, including public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and adjacent-stage private peers such as Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched.

Stage-progression methodology applies here as the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised ($52M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields $129M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or narrow-tier comparables within the semiconductor sector; only one adjacent-stage peer existed, below the three-datapoint threshold required for robust median triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $109M (low) to $148M (high), with a median point of $129M. This range reflects a single-method triangulation with 15% cushion bands around the stage-progression estimate. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific seed cohort, the absence of same-stage semiconductor comps, and the methodological reliance on historical capital raised rather than operating metrics or revenue. Additional data on burn rate, technical validation milestones, or market TAM would strengthen conviction in this range.
